gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the battery and water ratings were measured on different terms: Shokz's 12 h for the OpenRun Pro 2 and MOJAWA's 8 h for the Run Plus were both tested at 75% volume, Soundcore's 40/55 h for the Space One was tested at 50% volume, and the AeroFit 2 open-ear buds carry the same IP55 (not for water sports) as the OpenRun Pro 2, while only the Run Plus's IP68 is stated as good to 2 m for 2 hours.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no search and got no results or catalog cards, so there were no rival pages to compare against. Its answer has no battery hours, no test volumes and no IP ratings. It says only 'Running / cycling: Excellent' and makes no swim/IP distinction. Our own current page is wrong in two places this table fixes: it lists AeroFit 2 water resistance as 'Sweat resistant', but it is IP55, the same rating as the OpenRun Pro 2. It also lists the Run Plus at '10 h at 50%', but HeadphonesAddict measured 8 h 43 min at 50%.
decides: This confirms the split by use, and now with matched numbers. At the same 75% volume, the OpenRun Pro 2 runs 12 h against the Run Plus's 8 h, so for road running the Shokz lasts 50% longer per charge. But the OpenRun Pro 2 and the AeroFit 2 are both IP55, and Shokz says the OpenRun Pro 2 is not for water sports, so anyone who swims must take the MOJAWA (IP68, 2 m for 2 h). The Space One's 40 h with ANC is a 50%-volume figure, so it can't be set directly against the 75%-volume bone conduction numbers. Even so, it is about 3x or more on any basis, which keeps over-ears as the pick for desk and travel.
